clue.text: Boycott flag at game of cards

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as a union blacks goods
a jack is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: Someone boycotts a card game over a flag dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boycott' looks like the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack, also called pontoon or twenty-one, is a well-known casino card game.

clue.text: See 6
Boy repeating article on crop

indicators.note: repeating tells us to write the boy's name out twice in a row

parts.note: Alf is a short boy's name, from Alfred
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lad keeps going on about a farm crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, a fodder plant grown as a field crop for livestock, is another name for it.

clue.text: It's a bit audible at the roadside

indicators.note: audible says we want a word that sounds like the one the clue describes

parts.note: a curb is a type of bit, the chain or strap under a horse's jaw

explanation.surface: A small piece of something can be heard at the side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' looks like 'a little', but it is a horse's bit, the curb.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stone edge running along a pavement is the boundary of the road, at the roadside.

clue.text: A way for schools to organise money for charity

parts.note: LMS stands for Local Management of Schools, a British scheme letting schools run their own budgets

explanation.surface: A scheme lets schools raise funds for good causes.
explanation.walkthrough: LMS (Local Management of Schools) was a British policy of the 1990s giving schools control of their own budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts given to the poor are traditionally called this.

clue.text: Barbara is the top person at crosswords

parts.note: a king is the top person, the head of a realm
someone who does crosswords is a solver

explanation.surface: Barbara is praised as the champion crossword solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Kingsolver is an American novelist; her book appears at 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the American novelist Barbara Kingsolver serves to point at her surname.

clue.text: Prisoners keep start of year in Wales

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the prisoners surround the next letter

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Captives guard the beginning of the year in a Welsh jail.
explanation.walkthrough: POWYS is a large rural county in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a county located in Wales, so the clue's location points at it.

clue.text: Oops! Now I must be off, having lobbied erratically for 5's book

indicators.note: erratically means in a disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone apologises and leaves after canvassing clumsily for a novelist's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of OOPSNOWI and LOBBIED are rearranged; 'must be off, having' is surface padding. 5 is Barbara Kingsolver.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poisonwood Bible is Barbara Kingsolver's 1998 novel about a missionary family in the Congo.

clue.text: Where to get a drink problem in a brew

indicators.note: problem suggests the letters are in trouble and need sorting into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone with a drinking problem looks for a place to drink a brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink problem' reads as one phrase, but 'problem' is the anagram signal working on 'in a brew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar serving mainly wine is a place to go for a drink.

clue.text: Allurement of the French in part

indicators.note: in means the French word goes inside the word for part

parts.note: a section is a part
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: French charm in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is enticement or temptation, the act of luring someone.

clue.text: Speculation about supervisors — first one died (see above)

indicators.note: about means the word for speculation goes around the supervisors

parts.note: a bet is a speculation, a gamble
foremen supervise workers
first is 1, written as the Roman numeral I
taken as written
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Gossip about the bosses, then one of them died, as noted earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: '(see above)' is the definition: a reference to something already stated.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning stated earlier in a document, an instruction to look back to a previous passage.

clue.text: Fish cures, I've 'eard

indicators.note: the dropped h in 'eard says the word is said aloud in a Cockney accent with its h dropped

parts.note: heals means cures

explanation.surface: A Cockney says he has heard that fish are a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H from HEALS, as a Cockney would, and it sounds like EELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are snake-like fish.

clue.text: Dietetically valuable acid: you need nearly 20 — one in earlier years

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is left off the phrase for twenty

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: in means the one goes inside the years

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks earlier years
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diet guide says you need nearly twenty doses of an acid in early years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, an essential nutrient in the diet.

clue.text: Idiot gets infatuated with Yukon — this is absolutely true

indicators.note: infatuated suggests being besotted and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A fool falls in love with the Yukon, and swears it's true.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of IDIOT and YUKON are rearranged; 'gets' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase insisting a statement is honest and not a joke.

clue.text: Wrong valley, essential part of being alone

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a glen is a Scottish valley

indicators.note: part signals that only the opening piece of the word essential is kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A wicked valley holds the essential part of being alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential part' means the first three letters of 'essential'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Singleness is the state of being single, unmarried or on one's own.

clue.text: Butterfly (in place of white horse) with hawk reportedly in cold and looking it

indicators.note: in means the sound-alike goes inside the word for cold

parts.note: chill means cold

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a spelling that sounds like the hawk word

parts.note: hawk, said in a non-rhotic accent, is spelt here to fit
looking cold means looking blue

explanation.surface: A butterfly appears where a white horse is cut, with a hawk in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: White horses are giant figures cut into English chalk hillsides, the butterfly's habitat; 'hawk' said without its R gives the spelling needed. 'and' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalkhill blue is a pale blue British butterfly found on chalk downland.

clue.text: Shot holder when wagon reached high ground

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
a ridge is a long stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: A gun was loaded when the wagon reached the hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'reached' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is the casing holding the shot for a shotgun.

clue.text: Fighting back is the baroness

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: back means the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A baroness is fighting back.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Warsi is a British Conservative politician, a former party chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayeeda Warsi holds the title of baroness in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Stiff and cold with top removed

indicators.note: with top removed means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: frigid means cold

explanation.surface: Someone is stiff and cold after taking off their top.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending, firm and inflexible.

clue.text: Engage with King George over fruit

indicators.note: over in a down answer means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Engage with King George over some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with a problem is to engage with it or tackle it.

clue.text: New earring conceals attempt at chant

indicators.note: conceals means the rearranged earring holds the attempt inside
new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A new earring hides an effort at singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' could be read as a plain adjective on the earring, but it signals the rearrangement; 'conceals' wraps that around the attempt, and 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong named after Pope Gregory is a style of chant.

clue.text: Confiscate one thousand quid

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A fine of a thousand pounds is confiscated.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to seize and hold property by legal right.

clue.text: Thought out an issue in grass

indicators.note: in means the issue goes inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a is the indefinite article
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Someone thought out an issue while sitting in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned argument is one worked out logically.

clue.text: Address to cat in sound work

indicators.note: sound says the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: calling a cat '...' is addressing it

explanation.surface: Talking to a cat in a sound way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work.

clue.text: Weapon for society over fruit

indicators.note: over in a down answer means the society abbreviation sits above the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A society chooses a weapon over fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long throwing or thrusting weapon.

clue.text: Body on board is right

parts.note: a heavenly body placed before the word board makes the sailor's term for the right-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone on board ship says it is right.
explanation.walkthrough: STARBOARD is the right-hand side of a ship, so this heavenly body put on 'board' gives right.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a heavenly body.

clue.text: See 14 across
Deep end adapted for books on toenails, say, as for birds (those words being one)

definitions.text: as for birds (those words being one)

indicators.note: adapted means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: say means a word that sounds like the toenails word

parts.note: claws are birds' toenails

explanation.surface: Grammar notes on adapting a deep end for books about birds' toenails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as for birds' is itself a dependent clause, which is why the clue says those words make one; 'on' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause that cannot stand alone as a sentence; the clue's phrase is an example of one.

clue.text: East wind across the water, as it happens

parts.note: vent is French for wind, across the water meaning across the English Channel

explanation.surface: An east wind blows over the sea, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the water' means in France; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: Yield tear, there being less doubt about it

indicators.note: about means the less-doubt word wraps around the tear word

parts.note: surer means with less doubt
rend means tear

explanation.surface: A tear is yielded, with less doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: giving in or handing over to an opponent is yielding.
